item.title: SALSATECA FIESTA! — Sat Oct 31, 7:00 PM — WCKUK Lewisham
item.description: Your Salsa, Bachata and Cuban Party in Lewisham On the last Saturday of Every Month Learn Salsa, learn Bachata! Have fun and meet new friends!​ Our regular Saturdays become a party on the last Saturday of every month. Experience an unforgettable Salsa & Bachata Party at the Zhulin Hidden Village in Lewisham. We kick off the night with Salsa & Bachata lessons. If you’re new to dancing, we recommend joining our beginners’ group. All levels are welcome! No prior experience or dance partner is needed. Many attendees come solo, and we rotate partners throughout the lesson, giving you the chance to dance with different people. If you’d prefer to stay with your own partner for the entire class, just let the teacher know, and we’ll be happy to accommodate you. Since most Latin parties feature both Salsa and Bachata, learning both is not only fun but also a must! So, we strongly recommend and encourage our students to learn both. SCHEDULE: 7pm to 8pm: SALSA (Cross Body Style) Beginners

item.description:
Address: Check event page for more details.
On October 22, Anthopic and Theorem published LLMs are making formal software verification feasible at a much larger scale. This represents the first large-scale effort to use AI to apply formal verification to production software at the assembly code level.
Giles Edkins, software engineer at Epoch AI, will talk about what this result mean, and what it implies about software that we rely on today.
Doors open at 6:00 PM and the talk starts at 6:45 PM. Come early to grab a seat and say hi! Because of building security, someone from our team has to let each guest in, and once the talk begins…

item.title: Xuan Ji (CITA) — Wed Nov 4, 3:46 PM
item.description:
Title: How Orbital Eccentricity Erases Snowball Bistability on Earth-like Planets
Abstract: For the same stellar flux, Earth's climate can be either warm and partly ice-covered, or fully frozen in a "Snowball" state. This bistability comes from ice-albedo feedback: once ice forms, it reflects more sunlight and keeps itself frozen. A stable Snowball episode requires this bistability. Snowball episodes on Earth are linked to rises in atmospheric oxygen and in the complexity of life. I will start from the simplest global-mean energy balance model and show how ice-albedo feedback produces bifurcations and bistability. I will then turn to eccentric orbits. There, 3D global climate model simulations show the bistability disappears at moderate eccentricity. On the blackboard I will add ice thermodynamics to the energy balance model to explain why. This suggests Snowball episodes may be rarer on exoplanets than previously thought. Host: Soumendra Kishore Roy
Source: CITA Seminars
